axis_coverage.name: Original obligations and negative constraints
axis_coverage.semantic_analysis:
The final keeps rehearsal-room sound/decay/comfort separate from courtyard sound and the residents' experience. Its action criterion requires a repeatable receiver change; neither an indoor recording nor room reverberation can establish courtyard benefit. The published room/insulation/environmental standards have different subjects and do not provide a resident-defined universal threshold. See final lines 32–45 and 102–106; independent sources S01, S05 and S06.

It compares a source-output or agreed scheduling option with separate movable-panel, layout/source-position and specialist path-study options. Existing source controls, panels and a log-only fallback provide useful low-cost choices. A source inventory precedes selecting an amp control: the anecdote is not taken as proof that an amplifier exists. Scheduling changes exposure timing, not sound level. No construction, permanent installation, landlord enforcement, invented building material, complaint count, measurement or verified cause is recommended or asserted. Historical construction is described as comparator evidence, with its limits, rather than as the proposed intervention.

The main source A–B–A experiment is an outcome screen. It can establish whether a repeatable operating change helps the receiver under tested conditions; it cannot uniquely identify a physical route. The final accepts the draft's missing path-sensitive comparison and adds a conditional specialist branch with airborne-dominant and contact/impact-dominant excitation, source/receiver pressure and structural vibration observations. It expressly permits mixed paths and unresolved attribution. That meets the prospective observation obligation without inventing a dominant site path. The original design question does not require a measured or guaranteed diagnosis from hypothetical facts.

Real implementation histories and old-room-arrangement research opportunities are included. The final gives concrete questions for protocols, drawings, before/after evidence and receiver selection, with source/building/use/scale differences. A small omission of explicit historical operating-hour and concurrent-repair questions is recorded below; no historical causal improvement is claimed. The exact original plan appendix covers each prose/bullet clause, including authoring/release metadata without converting those into invented product obligations.

axis_coverage.name: Consequential source claims and applicability
axis_coverage.semantic_analysis:
I independently retrieved the governing primary records for all carried source identities S01–S14. The [independent source map](source-map.json) records exact URLs, versions, subjects/operations, units, domain limits, exceptions, candidate locators, access depth and navigable local evidence. S01–S06 were checked against official ISO public scopes/lifecycle or OBP preview. S07/S08 use publisher abstracts; S09/S12 author-institution records; S10 the complete EAA PDF text; S11 publisher-indexed paper text; S13/S14 complete first-party implementation pages. The original maps supplied identities, not proof. Direct HTTP failures are preserved separately from successful web/index retrievals.

The final's units and domains are correct: ISO 16283-1/-3 airborne insulation ranges are 50–5,000 Hz for intended 10–250 m³ rooms; S07's spatial variation is in dB, S11's absorber thickness in mm and room volume in m³. Environmental sound levels, room RT, airborne insulation, impact-source insulation and structural vibration remain distinct. No software/API default or value type is claimed. ISO 10052's survey method has higher uncertainty, a 150 m³ dwelling/comparable-room limit, octave-band insulation and special impact/service-equipment outputs; it does not make an improvised borrowed-meter test compliant. ISO 23591 covers differentiated music-rehearsal room acoustics/size, excludes insulation criteria and specialized concert/recording venues, and has a 2025 Gugak amendment. The final does not apply an out-of-scope numeric criterion.

Løvholt's 10–100 Hz wall/window model and laboratory comparisons support coupled air/structure behavior; the 15–30 Hz window and 30–100 Hz wall statements stay tied to those assemblies and source context. SINTEF's aircraft/lightweight-building record supports sound-induced floor vibration. Neither licenses a building-specific treatment, numerical benefit or route diagnosis from correlation. The final observes these conditions.

The residential-basement EAA paper explicitly excludes verification of proposed installed solutions, notwithstanding its later modeled objective-verification language. The final correctly treats it as a workflow analogue. The airbed record is a real lab-to-installation, before/after room-RT precedent, not a neighbor-noise experiment. UBC and Clore are real first-party implementation records, not independent performance trials; their public pages do not supply numeric after-results. Clore separately links BS4142 to plant noise and uses its baseline to set music-egress limits; the final does not misapply the plant rule to all music.

S11's carried URL now fails, and the accessible publisher-indexed alternative supplied the relevant substantive paper text. Its live alternative also fails. This is a locator/access limitation, not an unsupported substantive claim: the text explicitly supports the completed wind-band case, 1,600 m³ room, 40 mm prior absorbers, dry/imbalanced responses and overplaying. The candidate DOI was not independently exposed in the publisher text obtained, so its bibliographic confirmation remains limited. Full paywalled standards and most full journal papers were not read; public governing scopes/abstracts are sufficient for the bounded claims actually made, not for a future compliance test.

axis_coverage.name: Discovery, alternatives, analogues and history
axis_coverage.semantic_analysis:
The discovery contains useful unfamiliar findings rather than generic caution. Henry Wood Hall's lab-selected airbeds offer a flexible low-frequency room-decay precedent with installation and before/after measurement. The wind-band history shows that reducing room strength can coexist with overplaying and poor mutual hearing. Air-induced floor motion explains why vibration correlation can mislead path attribution. Low-frequency position effects motivate repeatable spatial sampling. The residential-basement bass/guitar/drum case supplies a close source-profile workflow while explicitly lacking installed-solution verification. UBC and Clore supply real measurement-to-design histories, project constraints and questions for commissioning evidence.

Competing options have different mechanisms and decision roles: source reduction changes excitation entering available routes; timing changes overlap with sensitive hours; relocation may change both radiation and contact; panels target reflections/decay; logs and quiet controls address source/event association; a specialist study can address path attribution when justified. Isolation/absorption concepts appear as histories or conditional diagnostics, with permanent work outside the proposal. No commercial product, new purchase or renovation design is required by the brief.

Room rearrangement remains an investigation opportunity: obtain dated records, plans, inventories and old/current user accounts, label recollection confidence, and avoid treating a new prospective pilot as an undocumented historical baseline. Follow-up asks about measurement positions, installation/use details, receiver objectives and before/after records. Differences between institutional/new-build/large-ensemble examples and the unknown small rehearsal building remain explicit. These are substantive leads with discriminating checks, not vacuous caveats.

axis_coverage.name: Criticism, corrections, rejections and dispositions
axis_coverage.semantic_analysis:
**CI-01 was a real material incompleteness in the investigator draft and is corrected in the final.** The draft called R3 preserved, but lowering a source changes excitation to all paths. Sound and floor motion can be correlated because airborne pressure excites surfaces. S08/S09 independently support the critic's objection. The final accepts it, preserves the original screen, and adds a proposed dominant-input contrast with synchronized observations and explicit limitations (final line 91 onward). It does not rewrite the lineage as already complete.

I also checked the added contrast independently against the official [ISO 16283-2:2020 scope](https://www.iso.org/standard/77436.html): impact-source pressure measurements are a distinct measurement concept from airborne room-to-room insulation. This corroborates the conceptual input distinction. It does not certify the candidate's improvised test, provide a courtyard route oracle, or guarantee clean path separation. The final's conditional specialist framing, spectrum documentation and mixed-path cautions are appropriate to those limits.

No wrong consequential correction, invented defect, false rejection or unanswered criticism was found. The critic's satisfied clause findings remain supported after independent checking. The critic's statement that no material wrong/unsupported claim remained is consistent with this review; its absence of a locator concern is qualified by the newly observed S11 access limitation. All nine categories of honestly unresolved external input remain in the final, including sensor/source-control access and musician acceptability. Detailed criticism dispositions are in assessment.json and the appendix.

axis_coverage.name: Meaning preservation across the pipeline
axis_coverage.semantic_analysis:
The final is self-contained. It preserves the original hypothetical facts, separate outcomes, coupled mechanisms, standards' scopes, source-transfer limits, main alternatives, real histories, owner/resident decisions, confounders, thresholds conditioned on measured variation, and distinction between desk work and proposed field checks. The disputed R3 wording is changed for an explicit reason, not silently discarded. It neither replaces the proposal with predecessor identifiers nor claims the literature settles the building.

Some nonmaterial detail was compressed or dropped. Discovery's optional direct/headphone-monitoring example using equipment already on hand, including the warning that pad/pedal impacts remain, disappears. The exact repeated 20-second EAA illustration and airbed inflation dependency are not repeated in the final. Historical operating-hour changes and simultaneous repairs are not explicit old-arrangement interview questions. These are real lineage/detail losses, not repairs I made or new obligations I invented. They do not remove a required option family, alter the supported provisional recommendation, produce an unsupported purchase or create a false historical conclusion. Source/schedule choices, repeated passages, history requests and the anti-attribution boundary remain meaningful.

axis_coverage.name: Proposed/executed validation and oracles
axis_coverage.semantic_analysis:
The proposed pilot specifies usual A, one-control B, repeated A–B–A blocks, quiet/no-rehearsal conditions, source inventory, separate indoor/outdoor records, calibration/settings/bandwidth checks, confounders and a receiver-tied reversible decision. If only the room improves, no courtyard benefit is claimed. The resident's audibility/disturbance/time concern and musicians' usable-room judgment are independent outcomes; pressure and vibration observations are evidence, not interchangeable proxies. No arbitrary universal numeric threshold or unperformed acoustic calculation is used.

Desk discovery/review and standards/version checks are reported as executed. The reviser specifically reports primary S08/S09 rechecks and its direct-open limitation. All interviews, complaint/event logging, inventory, source playback, calibration, measurements, panel/source tests, vibration observations, specialist diagnostics and standards-compliance checks are explicitly proposed or unexecuted. No field deployment, performance certification or successful intervention is invented. Original raw browser histories were not inspected; the assessment distinguishes authored execution claims and preserved maps from independently evidenced reviewer retrievals.

One basic meter plus a qualitative recorder cannot itself establish simultaneous calibrated observations at both sites and multiple interior positions. A sufficient multichannel or multi-instrument arrangement, sensor interface, access, response and repetitions must be specified when equipment is known. The final makes suitable equipment/access prerequisites and permits a log, screening or scoped specialist result, so it does not falsely assert current feasibility. The conditional contact/airborne contrast also requires safe comparable source states and appropriate sensors/analysis; it does not purport to create pure inputs. Honest unresolved external choices can pass at this proposal stage.
